_comment: Intended instruction-count changes between the merge-base and this branch head, each with its measured values and its cause. tools/check_instruction_counts.py accepts an out-of-tolerance operation ONLY if it appears here with matching numbers, and fails on an entry that no longer applies -- so this file cannot become a blanket exemption. An entry whose change the merge-base already contains (the reference measures its 'to': the state of every entry here once this branch merges) is reported as landed and excuses nothing; it stays true until its operation moves again. Same shape as benchmarks/check_baseline_justification.py requires of the wall-clock floors.
measured_on: containerised x86-64; avx512f/bw/cd/dq/ifma/vbmi/vl, vaes, vpclmulqdq, sha_ni; gcc -O2; AMA_DISPATCH_NO_AUTOTUNE=1; difference method at N=10

aes_256_gcm_encrypt.reason: Security hardening, paid for in instructions. The AES-256 key schedule and the GHASH accumulator are scrubbed at exit where gcc -O3 had hoisted them somewhere the source never named (INVARIANT-6), and the AEAD accept/reject return is masked rather than branched, pinned by an instruction-invariance gate.

dilithium_keygen.reason: ML-DSA gains the AVX2 NTT and shake256_x4 four-way absorb/squeeze for matrix expansion.

dilithium_sign.reason: DECLARED BREAKING CHANGE, not a performance regression. ama_dilithium_sign moved from ML-DSA.Sign_internal (FIPS 204 Algorithm 7, mu = H(tr || M), no domain separator) to the Sec 5.2 EXTERNAL interface (Algorithm 2), which prepends 0x00 || len(ctx) || ctx. That changes mu, which changes every rejection-sampling decision, so the loop runs a different number of times for any given key and message. Verified by measurement: the same seed yields an IDENTICAL public key on both sides but different signatures, and each side rejects the other's -- head sig VALID under head and INVALID under main, main sig VALID under main and INVALID under head. 4.x signatures do not verify under 5.0.0; this is the correction that makes the library interoperable with liboqs, BoringSSL, Go and Bouncy Castle. See CHANGELOG.md's BREAKING entry. The internal interface remains reachable as ama_ml_dsa_sign().

dilithium_verify.reason: Same AVX2 NTT and four-way SHAKE as dilithium_keygen.

ed25519_keygen.reason: The in-house Ed25519 backend replaces ed25519-donna: 5-bit signed comb with a constant-time masked select, an AVX2 fold for the 16-entry select, SHA-512 rounds unrolled x8, and Bernstein-Yang safegcd inversion.

ed25519_sign.reason: INVARIANT-51: the signer derives A = [a]B and refuses a key whose stored public half disagrees (2026-09 audit, B-2). Signing therefore does TWO fixed-base scalar multiplications where it did one -- the check is the same operation that computes R -- and that is the whole of the +103,629 Ir. Deliberate: without it, two signatures over ONE message under two different stored halves share R and give s1 - s2 = (h1 - h2) * a mod L, which recovers the private scalar, and a caller that stores the halves separately or rebuilds a key from a corrupted record reaches that input with no fault injector. The comparison itself is a laundered mask rather than a branch, so the output is masked and the verdict selected without a conditional -- worth about 130 Ir against the branching form CI measured at 331,941 on 84ad90d2, and it is what keeps ed25519-sign in the secret-taint lane that runs against the shipped shared object, where a declassification point expands to nothing. Supersedes the -9.32% entry, which described the Ed25519 rewrite before the check existed; that rewrite's saving is still in this number, under the doubled work.

ed25519_verify.reason: Half-size verification: Lehmer EEA reduces the scalar to ~128 bits and a four-way width-5/7 wNAF replaces the full double-scalar multiply.

hkdf_derive.reason: HKDF is extract-then-expand over HMAC-SHA3-256, so it inherits the Keccak gain.

hmac_sha3_256.reason: HMAC over the faster Keccak permutation. Two permutations per call, same -66%.

kyber_decapsulate.reason: Same AVX2 NTT and reciprocal-multiply change; decapsulation also runs the FO re-encryption, which is why its gain is the smallest of the three.

kyber_encapsulate.reason: Same AVX2 NTT and reciprocal-multiply change as kyber_keygen.

kyber_keygen.reason: ML-KEM gains the AVX2 NTT and the KyberSlash divisions are replaced by an exact Granlund-Montgomery reciprocal multiply, proven byte-identical over all 16,645 (coefficient, width) pairs.

sha3_256.reason: Keccak-f[1600] gains the AVX2/AVX-512 kernels and the BMI1/BMI2 scalar path; this branch is where the SIMD SHA3 work lands. All four Keccak-driven rows move by the same -66%, which is the signature of one shared kernel rather than four separate changes.

sha3_512.reason: Same Keccak kernel as sha3_256; the -66% matches to two decimal places, which is what a shared permutation should look like.

x25519_scalarmult.reason: No change to the X25519 code path: the ladder, its inputs and its source are unchanged. The Release archive is built with -flto, and the driver link re-optimises every translation unit together, so edits to units X25519 never calls move its count. Bisected on dcc8ab9 (1,115,771 Ir) by adding this pass's files one at a time: src/c/ama_consttime.c (the internal stack-wipe helper) takes it to 1,099,706, and src/c/dispatch/ama_dispatch.c (the AMA_DISPATCH_ONLY pin and cache-diagnostic edits) to 1,073,681. Recorded because the gate is right that the executed instruction stream changed; nothing here is a regression.
